extracted.intended_audience: acute care hospital administrators, hospital compliance officers, health policy stakeholders, and other entities affected by Medicare episode-based payment models (CJR-X)
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Medicare rule defining who must participate in the Comprehensive Care for Joint Replacement Expanded (CJR‑X) model, which beneficiaries and services are included, episode identification and timing, beneficiary notification requirements, and related operational and statutory requirements for nationwide expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance year timing
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X performance years would align with fiscal years (FYs); first PY proposed to run from October 1, 2027 through September 30, 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considered calendar year alignment but proposes FY alignment because IPPS is aligned to an FY cycle and future policy changes would be proposed in the IPPS rulemaking cycle. CMS seeks comment on defining 'performance year' as aligning with FYs and the proposed October 1, 2027 start date; alternative start dates also solicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory participation for eligible acute care hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participation would be mandatory for all eligible acute care hospitals nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This differs from the original CJR Model (which was mandatory within selected MSAs). CMS proposes mandating all eligible acute care hospitals that meet the 'CJR‑X participant' definition; comments requested on proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'hospital' for CJR‑X
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'hospital' as in section 1886(d)(1)(B) of the Act, which includes only acute care hospitals and excludes certain specialty hospitals (e.g., psychiatric and cancer hospitals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS seeks comment on adopting this statutory definition at §512.605 to limit CJR‑X to acute care hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'CJR‑X participant'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'CJR‑X participant' is an acute care hospital located in any State, DC, or U.S. Territory that initiates LEJR episodes and is paid under both the IPPS and OPPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals that do not meet both IPPS and OPPS payment status (for example, IHS/Tribal hospitals, Rural Community Hospital Demonstration participants, Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Emergency Hospitals) would be excluded to avoid challenges constructing target prices for episodes that initiate in outpatient or inpatient departments but are not paid under both systems. CJR‑X participants remain participants unless they no longer meet the definition, CMS terminates CJR‑X, or they receive notice of termination under §512.165.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant exceptions — TEAM participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude hospitals that are TEAM participants from CJR‑X while TEAM is in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: TEAM tests 30‑day LEJR episodes while CJR‑X would test 90‑day episodes; exclusion preserves comparability and avoids confusion from dual rules. Exclusion applies to mandatory and voluntary TEAM participants and expires at TEAM conclusion or if a TEAM participant no longer meets TEAM participation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant exceptions — Maryland hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to exclude acute care hospitals in the State of Maryland because of Maryland's unique rate‑setting authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes regional pricing methodology in CJR‑X would not accurately reflect Maryland hospitals' episode spending. Acknowledges Maryland's AHEAD model participation and potential transition of rate‑setting authority; CMS may consider future modifications through rulemaking to permit concurrent participation or other changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory findings required to expand model nationally (section 1115A(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before expansion, the Secretary must find: (1) expansion is expected to reduce spending without reducing quality or improve quality without increasing spending; (2) CMS Chief Actuary certifies expansion would reduce (or not increase) net program spending; (3) expansion would not deny or limit coverage or provision of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS must take into account the evaluation of the model under section 1115A(b)(4) when making these findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics demonstrating maintained quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of care is assessed by metrics such as emergency department (ED) visits, unplanned readmission rates, mortality rates, and LEJR complication rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CJR Model evaluation showing $112.7 million net Medicare savings across PYs 6 and 7 while maintaining quality on these measures underpins the Secretary's determination to expand the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary is included in CJR‑X if at admission for an anchor procedure/hospitalization they: (a) are enrolled in Medicare Part A and Part B; (b) have Medicare as primary payer; (c) are not eligible for Medicare due to end‑stage renal disease; (d) are not enrolled in any managed care plan; (e) are not covered under a United Mine Workers of America health plan; and (f) are in an episode as defined at §512.605.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria align with the CJR Model population and ensure CMS has complete and consistent claims data across the full episode. Excluding managed care and other non‑IPPS/OPPS payments reduces heterogeneity and preserves comparability across episodes and hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode cancellation if beneficiary ceases to meet inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: If a beneficiary included in an episode ceases to meet the beneficiary inclusion criteria during the episode, CMS proposes to cancel the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal located at §512.620(b); CMS seeks comment on this cancellation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary notification requirement — hospital responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Every CJR‑X participant must provide written notification to each CJR‑X beneficiary of his or her inclusion in the CJR‑X model prior to discharge from the anchor hospitalization or anchor procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must explain the model and how it may affect care; inform beneficiaries of freedom of choice; explain how beneficiaries can access care records and claims data (e.g., patient portal, Blue Button®); explain that CJR‑X participants may receive beneficiary‑identifiable claims data; advise beneficiaries that standard Medicare protections remain and how to report concerns; and provide a list of CJR‑X collaborators or a web address where that list is publicly available. CMS recognizes timing constraints and invites comment on timing and source of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary notification requirement — collaborator responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must require every CJR‑X collaborator to provide written notice to applicable beneficiaries describing the existence of the sharing arrangement and the basic quality and payment incentives under the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborator notice must be provided no later than the time the beneficiary first receives an item or service from the collaborator during an episode; if not feasible due to patient condition, the notice must be provided as soon as reasonably practicable. CMS would post a CJR‑X collaborator template if policy is finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification delivery flexibility (web link for collaborator list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals may fulfill the requirement to provide a list of CJR‑X collaborators by including a publicly available web address where beneficiaries can access the collaborators list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is allowed because exhaustive lists may lengthen notifications unnecessarily. CMS balances completeness of information against administrative burden and beneficiary information overload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on steering and fees for preferred providers
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants may recommend preferred providers but may not limit beneficiaries to a preferred or recommended provider list inconsistent with statutes/regulations; participants may not charge any CJR‑X collaborator a fee to be included on any list of preferred providers, nor accept such payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations must comply with current law and beneficiary freedom of choice protections. Charging for placement or accepting payments for inclusion would be outside the realm of permitted risk‑sharing agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode definition — time window and included items/services
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'episode' means all Medicare Part A and B items and services furnished to an included beneficiary beginning on the date of admission to an anchor hospitalization or the date of the anchor procedure and ending on the 90th day following discharge (date of discharge or procedure counted as first day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with CJR Model and TEAM definitions. CMS emphasizes clinically similar episodes and episodes with significant post‑acute spending to maximize care redesign opportunities. Episodes include all Part A and B services during the 90‑day post‑discharge period, subject to proposed exclusions in §512.625(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode identification methodology (MS‑DRG/HCPCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: LEJR episodes would be identified by the MS‑DRG of the anchor hospitalization or by HCPCS codes for hospital outpatient procedures (operational simplicity and consistency with past models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically proposed triggers: IPPS discharges under MS‑DRG 469, 470, 521, or 522; OPPS claims for HCPCS 27130 (total hip arthroplasty) or 27447 (total knee arthroplasty). CMS recognizes that final MS‑DRG assignment may change after discharge; in those instances, participants could rely on CMS data shared under a data sharing agreement and attestation to confirm attribution. CMS seeks comment on identifying episodes via MS‑DRGs and HCPCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode scope — included procedure types and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X LEJR episodes would include inpatient hip, knee, and ankle replacement procedures paid through IPPS (select MS‑DRGs) and hospital outpatient hip and knee replacement procedures billed under select HCPCS codes through OPPS; outpatient ankle replacements (total ankle arthroplasty, TAA) would be excluded from CJR‑X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outpatient TAAs were not included because TAA was on the IPO list until 2021 and thus not included in prior models; outpatient TAAs are being tested in TEAM (HCPCS 27702) and could be considered for future inclusion in CJR‑X via notice and comment if TEAM evaluation supports it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode initiation rules and transfer handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode begins on outpatient procedure date for outpatient anchors and on admission date for inpatient anchors; if an anchor hospitalization occurs on same day or within 3 days of an outpatient LEJR procedure, begin episode on the outpatient procedure date. Transfers: if initial inpatient admission is for an included MS‑DRG, a transfer does not initiate a new anchor hospitalization; if a beneficiary is transferred and the second hospitalization has an included MS‑DRG while the first did not, the second hospitalization would initiate the episode at the receiving hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with CJR Model and Medicare 3‑day payment guidelines requiring bundling of related outpatient services occurring within 3 days of an inpatient admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items and services specifically included (non‑exhaustive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of items and services included in an episode: physicians' services; inpatient hospital services (IPPS operating and capital payments); inpatient psychiatric facility (IPF) services; LTCH services; IRF services; SNF services; HHA services; hospital outpatient services; outpatient therapy; clinical laboratory; durable medical equipment; Part B drugs and biologics except those excluded under §512.625(c); hospice services; Part B professional claims dated in the 3 days prior to an anchor hospitalization if the outpatient procedure was not detected as part of the hospitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including these services promotes comprehensive, coordinated accountability for the full continuum of care and avoids fragmenting financial responsibility, which could undermine care coordination and cost containment goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational simplicity and consistency with prior models
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS favors straightforward episode identification and policies consistent with CJR Model and BPCI Advanced (e.g., using MS‑DRGs/HCPCS codes and a 90‑day post‑discharge window) to facilitate care redesign and participant operational readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes hospitals often have prior experience with episode‑based payment models and that consistent methods (MS‑DRG/HCPCS triggers, 90‑day episodes) support provider operational simplicity and CMS program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing to confirm episode attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: In instances where an episode‑initiating code changes after discharge and the episode would not be picked up, CJR‑X participants could rely on data shared by CMS under a CJR‑X data sharing agreement and attestation to confirm episode attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS describes this as a mechanism to address potential attribution discrepancies due to changes in final MS‑DRG assignment following claims processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of beneficiary protections with administrative burden
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes beneficiary notification requirements and other protections (freedom of choice, reporting mechanisms) but recognizes potential redundancy and information overload; CMS invites comment on whether notification requirements should be required only during years when both CJR‑X and TEAM are implemented or whether notification should be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS weighed that national expansion could normalize practices and that beneficiaries already receive discharge information; thus, benefits of additional notification must be balanced against administrative burden and potential for the notification to go unnoticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on financial steering through collaborator lists
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants may recommend preferred providers but may not limit beneficiaries to a preferred list inconsistent with law; participants cannot charge collaborators to be on a preferred list nor accept such payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition preserves beneficiary freedom of choice and prevents financial incentives that would be considered outside permitted risk‑sharing arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with prior model evaluation and stakeholder feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of CJR‑X that differ from the original CJR Model or CJR Extension were included based on evaluation findings from CJR and BPCI Advanced and stakeholder feedback, including responses to prior Requests for Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes minor modifications in CJR‑X to align with policies implemented in TEAM where those represent improvements to CJR methodology (as discussed in FY 2025 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule). CMS seeks comment on these alignments and modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for hospitals with special payment status
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals that are not paid under both IPPS and OPPS (for example, IHS/Tribal hospitals, Rural Community Hospital Demonstration participants, Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Emergency Hospitals) would be excluded from CJR‑X participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: excluding these hospitals avoids problems constructing target prices for episodes that initiate in inpatient or outpatient settings but lack the corresponding payment system coverage, preserving fairness and data completeness.
